landmarks.name: Itaipu Dam
landmarks.writeup: One of the world's largest hydroelectric dams, located on the Paraná River between Paraguay and Brazil.

landmarks.name: Jesuit Missions of La Santísima Trinidad de Paraná
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site featuring well-preserved ruins of a 17th-century Jesuit mission.

landmarks.name: Palacio de los López
landmarks.writeup: The presidential palace in Asunción, known for its neoclassical architecture and historical significance.

cultural_events.name: Festival del Lago Ypacaraí
cultural_events.writeup: An annual music and cultural festival celebrating Paraguayan folklore and traditions near Lake Ypacaraí.

cultural_events.name: Ñandutí Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A festival honoring the traditional Paraguayan lace-making craft called Ñandutí.

food_writeup: Paraguayan cuisine features staples like mandioca (cassava), corn, and beef, with popular dishes including sopa paraguaya (cornbread), chipa (cheese bread), and mbejú (starch pancake).
brief_history: Paraguay gained independence from Spain in 1811. It experienced significant conflict during the War of the Triple Alliance (1864-1870) and the Chaco War (1932-1935). The country has a history of political instability but has been democratic since 1989.
current_conflicts: Paraguay is generally stable with no major ongoing conflicts, though it faces challenges related to border security and organized crime.
